div.head: MEMB. 4.
SUBSECT. 1.
Physician, Patient, Physic.
div.p:
Of those diverse gifts which our Apostle Paul saith, God hath bestowed on man, this of Physic is not the least, but most necessary, and especially conducing to the good of mankind. Next therefore to God in all our extremities (for of the most high cometh healing, Ecclus. 38. 2) we must seek to, and rely upon the Physician, Ecclus. 38. In the sight of great men he shall be in admiration.who is Manus Dei [the hand of God], saith Herophilus, and to whom he hath given knowledge, that he might be glorified in his wondrous works. With such doth he heal men, and taketh away their pains, Ecclus. 38. 6, 7, when thou hast need of him, let him not go from thee. The hour may come that their enterprises may have good success, ver. 13. It is not therefore to be doubted, that if we seek a Physician as we ought, we may be eased of our infirmities, such a one I mean as is sufficient, and worthily so called; for there be many Mountebanks, Quacksalvers, Empirics, in every street almost, and in every village, that take upon them this name, make this noble and profitable Art to be evil spoken of and contemned, by reason of these base and illiterate Artificers: but such a Physician I speak of, as is approved, learned, skilful, honest, &c., of whose duty Wecker, Antid. cap. 2 & Syntax. med., Crato, Julius Alexandrinus lib. de med., Heurnius prax. med. lib. 3 cap. 1, &c., treat at large. For this particular disease, him that shall take upon him to cure it, Tom. 4 Tract. 1, de morbis amentium. Horum multi non nisi a Magis curandi & Astrologis, quoniam origo ejus a coelis petenda est [Many of these are only to be cured by magicians and astrologers, because their origin is to be sought in the heavens].Paracelsus will have to be a Magician, a Chemist, a Philosopher, an Astrologer; Thurneisserus, Severinus the Dane, and some other of his followers, require as much: many of them cannot be cured but by Magic. Lib. de Podagra.Paracelsus is so stiff for those Chemical medicines, that in his cures he will admit almost of no other Physic, deriding in the meantime Hippocrates, Galen, and all their followers: but Magic, and all such remedies I have already censured, & shall speak of Chemistry Sect. 5.elsewhere. Astrology is required by many famous Physicians, by Ficinus, Crato, Fernelius, Langius. J. Caesar Claudinus consult.doubted of, and exploded by others: I will not take upon me to decide the controversy myself, Johannes Hasfurtus, Thomas Boderius, and Maginus in the preface to his Mathematical physic, shall determine for me. Many Physicians explode Astrology in physic (saith he), there is no use of it, vanam artem ac quasi temerariam insectantur, ac gloriam sibi ab ejus imperitia aucupantur [they censure it as an empty and imprudent art, and seek praise for being ignorant of it]; but I will reprove Physicians by Physicians, that defend and profess it, Hippocrates, Galen, Avicenna, &c., that count them butchers without it, homicidas medicos Astrologiae ignaros, &c. [murderous physicians ignorant of
astrology, etc.] Paracelsus goes farther, and will have his Physician predestinated to this man’s cure, this malady; and time of cure, the scheme of each geniture inspected, gathering of herbs, of administering, Astrologically observed; in which Thurneisserus, and some Iatromathematical professors, are too superstitious in my judgement. Hellebore will help, but not always, not given by every Physician, &c., but these men are too peremptory and self-conceited as I think. But what do I do, interposing in that which is beyond my reach? A blind man cannot judge of colours, nor I peradventure of these things. Only thus much I would require, Honesty in every Physician, that he be not over-careless or covetous, Harpy-like to make a prey of his patient; Carnificis namque est (as Antid. gen. lib. 3 cap. 2.Wecker notes) inter ipsos cruciatus ingens precium exposcere [for it’s the nature of an executioner … to demand a huge payment from someone in the midst of his affliction], as an hungry Chirurgeon often produce and wire-draw his cure, so long as there is any hope of pay,

lg.l: Non missura cutem, nisi plena cruoris hirudo.
[A leech that won’t let go of the skin, unless it’s full of blood.]

div.p:
Many of them to get a fee, will give Physic to everyone that comes, when there is no cause, and they do so irritare silentem morbum, as Quod saepe evenit, lib. 3 cap. 1, cum non sit necessitas. Frustra fatigant remediis aegros, qui victus ratione curari possunt [Which often happens … when it’s not necessary. With medicines they uselessly tire out patients who could be cured by a methodical regimen]. Heurnius.Heurnius complains, stir up a silent disease, as it often falleth out, which by good counsel, good advice alone, might have been happily composed, or by rectification of those six non-natural things otherwise cured. This is Naturae bellum inferre, to oppugn nature, & to make a strong body weak. Arnaldus in his 8th & 11th Aphorisms gives cautions against, and expressly forbiddeth it. 11 Aphor.A wise Physician will not give Physic, but upon necessity, and first try medicinal diet, before he proceed to medicinal cure. Brev. lib. 1 cap. 18.In another place he laughs those men to scorn, that think longis syrupis expugnare daemones & animi phantasmata, they can purge fantastical imaginations, & the devil by physic. Another caution is, that they proceed upon good grounds, if so be there be need of Physic, and not mistake the disease; they are often deceived by the similitude of Symptoms, saith Heurnius, and I could give instance in many Consultations, wherein they have prescribed opposite Physic. Sometimes they go too perfunctorily to work, in not prescribing a just Qui melancholicis praebent remedia non satis valida. Longiores morbi imprimis solertiam medici postulant, & fidelitatem, qui enim tumultuarie hos tractant, vires absque ullo commodo laedunt & frangunt, &c. [Those who supply melancholics with remedies that are not effective enough. Diseases of longer duration principally require skill and accuracy from the doctor: those who treat them haphazardly damage and diminish the physical powers without any benefit, etc.]course of Physic: to stir up the humour, and not to purge it, doth often more harm than good. Montanus consil. 30 inveighs against such perturbations, that purge to the halves, tire nature, and molest the body to no
purpose. ’Tis a crabbed humour to purge, and as Laurentius calls this disease, the reproach of Physicians; Besardus, flagellum medicorum, their lash; & for that cause, more carefully to be respected. Though the patient be averse, saith Laurentius, desire help, and refuse it again, though he neglect his own health, it behoves a good Physician, not to leave him helpless. But most part they offend in that other extreme, they prescribe too much physic, and tire out their bodies with continual potions, to no purpose. Aetius tetrabib. 2 ser. 2 cap. 90 will have them by all means therefore to give some respite to nature, to leave off now and then; & Laelius à Fonte Eugubinus in his consultations, found it (as he there witnesseth) often verified by experience, that after a deal of Physic to no purpose, left to themselves, they have recovered. ’Tis that which Nic. Piso, Donatus Altomarus, still inculcate, dare requiem Naturae, to give nature rest.
